answer: Split the identity ledger into 64 shards and require each shard to publish a signed sonnet of every account it admits. A node can only act in shards where it has been admitted, and each new shard entry costs a rising dune of stake that compounds with the number of shards already held, so a farm that wants one puppet in each of 64 shards pays a geometrically growing bond instead of a flat fee. Auditors lantern-check every shard admission against the other 63 shards' signatures at each close, so an account admitted twice is caught before it can vote twice.
